integrated_description: Immediately pause and conduct an explicit 30–60 second safety and needs check, asking directly: 'Are you safe?' and 'What kind of support do you need right now?' If there is any indication of danger (self-harm, severe panic, or medical risk), notify teammates in one brief message and exit immediately, calling for emergency support if needed. If the situation is serious but not dangerous, the default response is to pause and exit for full presence — the only exception being if the roommate explicitly confirms they can tolerate a short wait, in which case complete only a clearly bounded, minimal in-game action (no more than 2–3 minutes, not an indeterminate segment), deliver a concrete time commitment ('I will be with you in X minutes'), and then provide uninterrupted, committed support for a defined window (5–10 minutes minimum), with an explicit assurance throughout that the roommate will not be left alone.
integration_rationale: All three modifications are reconciled by replacing the vague 'current in-game segment' condition with a roommate-consent-based exception (stakeholder_b), making the triage an explicit safety-and-needs check with concrete timing and a defined support window (stakeholder_a and stakeholder_c), and establishing immediate exit as the default rather than a threshold tied solely to danger level.
